html:
The April 9 tragedy was the breaking up of a peaceful independence protest in Tbilisi by Soviet troops early on 9 April 1989, in which 21 people, most of them young women, were killed.

Thousands had gathered for days outside the government building on Rustaveli Avenue, demanding independence and opposing Abkhaz separatists. Soldiers attacked with sharpened spades and tear gas. The killings shocked the Soviet Union and destroyed the communist party's standing in Georgia. Within two years Georgia declared independence, on 9 April 1991, under the nationalist Zviad Gamsakhurdia. The day is now the Day of National Unity in Georgia, and it was a step toward the war in Abkhazia that followed.
sum: The April 9 tragedy was the breaking up of a peaceful independence protest in Tbilisi by Soviet troops early on 9 April 1989, in which 21 people, most of them young women, were killed.
